overview.description: Grow materials and objects instead of manufacturing them: engineered living materials, mycelium composites, bacterial cellulose, and biofabricated design. This module bridges biology and design - treating living systems as a fabrication substrate with its own constraints of growth, scale, and sustainability.
objectives: design an object or material to be grown, not built
weigh scale, reproducibility, and sustainability trade-offs
integrate engineered biology with design intent

steps.description: Choose a living material, define the growth process and mould/scaffold, cultivate under controlled conditions, then post-process into a finished form.
steps.intro: Biofabrication is design with a partner that grows: you set conditions and boundaries, and the organism builds the material.
tools: a living material system (mycelium / Komagataeibacter for cellulose)

instructions.title: Choose the material & form
instructions.description: Pick a system (mycelium composite, bacterial cellulose, etc.) and the object/material properties you want.

instructions.title: Prepare substrate & scaffold
instructions.description: Formulate the substrate and build a mould or scaffold that guides growth into the target shape.

instructions.title: Cultivate
instructions.description: Inoculate and grow under controlled, contamination-free conditions until the material sets.

instructions.title: Finish & evaluate
instructions.description: Dry/press/treat the material, then evaluate strength, reproducibility, and sustainability against the design goal.

submission.description: Propose a biofabricated object or material: the organism/system, the growth-and-mould process, and an honest assessment of scale and sustainability.

kits.name: Grow-It-Yourself mycelium material kit
kits.note: Grow a solid mushroom-material object in a mould - biofabrication you can hold.

kits.name: Bacterial cellulose (kombucha SCOBY)
kits.note: Grow a leather-like cellulose sheet from a SCOBY culture - cheapest living material.
